slot.brief: Solve a first-order linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) where P is a simple function (e.g., 1/x or a constant) via the integrating factor; possibly with an initial condition.

verdicts.working: Multiplying by the integrating factor x gives (xy)' = x ln x. Integrating: xy = (x²/2) ln x − x²/4 + C. The initial condition gives C = 5/4, hence y(2) = ln 2 + 1/8.

working:
Integrating factor $=x$: $(xy)'=x\ln x$. Hence $xy=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\dfrac{x^2}{4}+C$. From $y(1)=1$, $C=\dfrac54$. Thus $y(2)=\ln2-\dfrac12+\dfrac58=\ln2+\dfrac18$.

solution:
The integrating factor is $x$, so $(xy)'=x\ln x$.
$$xy=\frac{x^2}{2}\ln x-\frac{x^2}{4}+C$$
Using $y(1)=1$ gives $C=\frac54$. Hence $y(2)=\ln 2-\frac12+\frac58=\ln 2+\frac18$.
